name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs for two weeks first. This gives us real-world data on its impact without disrupting workflows, letting us measure actual improvements before committing. The trade-off is temporary overhead—extra logs and monitoring—but the risk of breaking anything is zero since it runs in read-only mode. After two weeks, we’ll have hard numbers to decide if it’s worth full adoption.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode risks normalizing false negatives as "acceptable" because it never forces us to confront PR-Agent’s actual failures—just logs them. A better alternative is running it in *parallel mode* on a subset of PRs for two weeks, where maintainers manually verify every suggestion before merging; this exposes real flaws while keeping risk near zero. Settle it by tracking both false positives *and* false negatives, and requiring a lead’s explicit sign-off on any auto-applied changes after the test.
